c.tagline: Russia's Baltic exclave, Kant's Königsberg reborn in amber and brick.

taxi.fareNote: Most people book via the Yandex Go app, which gives a fixed up-front price; street taxis usually negotiate a fare rather than run a meter, with a minimum charge of around 100 rubles.

emergency.note: 112 is the single all-services emergency number; 102 reaches police and 103 an ambulance directly.

avoid.reason: Watch belongings around the Central Market and late-night bar areas, and never photograph military or port installations in this heavily militarized region.

hood_desc: The modern civic center around Victory Square (Ploshchad Pobedy), with the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, Leninsky Prospekt shopping, hotels, malls, and restaurants; the convenient walkable base for first-timers.

The touristy 'Fishing Village' of red-roofed, German-style buildings along the Pregolya opposite Kant Island and Königsberg Cathedral, full of cafes, hotels, and river views; the picturesque sightseeing quarter.
A leafy pre-war German villa district west of the center with cobbled streets and preserved Jugendstil mansions that survived the war; quiet, elegant, and residential.
A historic garden-suburb on the north-east edge of the center around the Upper Pond (Verkhneye Lake), with old villas, parks, and a calm, upscale residential feel.
A large marshy island in the Pregolya being redeveloped around the 2018 World Cup stadium and new embankments; open, modern, and green, quieter than the historic core.

water.note: Tap water quality is unreliable; drink bottled or boiled water.

transit.hours: Trams, trolleybuses, buses, and marshrutkas run roughly 06:00 to 23:00; frequencies drop in the evening.
transit.note: Kaliningrad has an extensive surface network of buses, marshrutka minibuses, trolleybuses, and one of Russia's oldest tram systems. The compact center around the Cathedral, Fishing Village, and Victory Square is walkable.
transit.pay: Flat fares are paid in cash to the conductor or driver on board (around 30-35 rubles); contactless bank-card payment is accepted on many routes. There is no zonal system.

bus: International coaches to Gdańsk, Vilnius, and beyond (services vary)
Regional buses across Kaliningrad Oblast (Svetlogorsk, Zelenogradsk, Curonian Spit)
ferry: Seasonal boat services on the Vistula Lagoon; commercial sea port on the Pregolya
train: Kaliningrad-Passazhirsky (South Station): long-distance trains to Moscow (~22 h) and St Petersburg via Belarus/Lithuania
Regional elektrichka trains to Svetlogorsk, Zelenogradsk, and Baltiysk

transit.m: Express bus 244E to the city center / South Station (~40-50 min, roughly hourly)

tip.r: Not obligatory; leaving around 10% for good service in restaurants is common and appreciated.
